title: Their proof from Acts 17:28: in him we live and move and are
source_text: V. Illud autem colligunt ex quibusdam Scripturae locis. Praecipuus ille est qui habetur Act. 17. 28. In ipso vivimus & movemur & sumus. Quum enim dicit Apostolus nos in Deo, id est, per illum & esse & vivere, satis docet Deum esse qui & naturam & facultates omnes nobis initio dedit & jugiter conservat; adeoque quum addit nos quoque in Deo moveri, plane docere videtur omnes nostros motus atque actiones sicut naturam ipsam, immediate a Deo procedere, & Virtute illius fieri.
pass_a_gloss: And this they gather from certain places of Scripture. The chief is that which is had Acts 17. 28. In him we live and move and are. For when the Apostle says that we in God, that is, through him both are and live, he sufficiently teaches that it is God who both gave us nature and all faculties at the beginning and continually preserves them; and so when he adds that we also are moved in God, he seems plainly to teach that all our motions and actions, like nature itself, proceed immediately from God, and are done by his Power.
pass_b_english: They draw this from certain passages of Scripture, chiefly Acts 17:28: 'In him we live and move and have our being.'

When the Apostle says that we exist and live in God, that is, through him, he makes it clear enough that God gave us our nature and all our powers at the start and constantly sustains them. And when he adds that we also move in God, he appears to teach outright that all our movements and actions, like our nature itself, come directly from God and are carried out by his power.

choices.why: The Schools' term for God's acting together with secondary causes; 'concurrence' keeps it recognizable as the technical term, with 'cooperation' kept for cooperatio.
